description: A litigation director must approve a resolution package for a former sales manager's discrimination claim, including the settlement amount, mediation condition, personnel-record treatment, and employment reference terms, with input from human resources and the company's employment-practices insurer.

shared_context.S1: A former sales manager has asserted discrimination and retaliation claims against the company and demanded $180,000 to resolve them.
shared_context.S2: A mediation is scheduled for next Wednesday, and Elena Morris must approve the company's final resolution authority and settlement terms before the mediation.
shared_context.S3: The former employee's personnel file currently states that the employee was terminated for performance reasons.
shared_context.S4: Under the legal team's normal settlement-preparation process, Elena conducts a pre-mediation review with HR and insurance claims counsel and asks each for any relevant case or coverage information before setting the resolution package.
shared_context.S5: This meeting is the required decision point: after HR and insurance claims counsel have reported their relevant information, Elena must record the final resolution authority and settlement terms before the meeting ends, without scheduling another review or requesting outside follow-up work.

PF1.text: During a confidential exit-resolution call this week, the former employee's counsel stated that the employee will accept a settlement only if the personnel record is changed to state 'resigned in good standing' and the company provides a neutral reference limited to dates of employment and last job title; Daniel recorded this in his HR notes, but it is not yet in the shared case summary.

PF2.text: The employment-practices insurer confirmed by email this week that it authorizes exactly $95,000 inclusive of defense costs for this claim, requires completion of mediation before execution, and requires the insurer's written consent to the final settlement agreement; Marisol has not uploaded the email because she was waiting to confirm the authority with the claims examiner.

acceptance_conditions: The resolution authority must be exactly $95,000 inclusive of defense costs.
Mediation must be completed before the settlement agreement is executed.
The personnel record must be changed to state 'resigned in good standing'.
The company must provide a neutral reference limited to dates of employment and last job title.
The final settlement agreement must require the insurer's written consent.
The insurer's authority must be cited as justification for the settlement amount.

content_checks.C4: decisions['reference_scope'] == 'neutral reference limited to dates of employment and last job title'
content_checks.C7: decisions['reference_scope'] == 'neutral reference limited to dates of employment and last job title'

decisive_facts.why: The existing file says termination for performance reasons and no reference terms are set; PF1 changes the required record language to 'resigned in good standing' and the reference to dates of employment and last job title.

The $180,000 demand and scheduled mediation provide no exact authority or insurer condition; PF2 changes the approved amount to exactly $95,000, requires mediation before execution, and requires written insurer consent.
